questions.prompt: After a short coffee break we ____ with the meeting.
questions.explanation: “Carried on” means continued. The meeting resumed after the break.

questions.prompt: I hate to ____ this subject now, but do you have the money you owe me?
questions.explanation: “Bring up” means introduce a topic into a conversation. The speaker introduces the subject of the debt.

questions.prompt: If you are tired, ____ take a nap on my bed.
questions.explanation: “By all means” gives permission or encouragement. The speaker welcomes the other person to take a nap.

questions.prompt: My uncle is generous, but he ____ lending money to relatives.
questions.explanation: “Draws the line at” sets a limit. He is generous but will not lend money to relatives.

questions.prompt: She can be very scary when she ____.
questions.explanation: “Loses her temper” means becomes angry. Her anger can frighten people.

questions.prompt: ____, I found ten dollars under the table at the restaurant.
questions.explanation: “By chance” means accidentally or without planning. Finding the money was unexpected.

questions.prompt: The bus driver ____ because one of the passengers got sick.
questions.explanation: “Pulled over” means moved the vehicle to the side of the road and stopped.

questions.prompt: They wanted to ____ the old apartment, but they did not have enough money.
questions.explanation: “Fix up” means repair or improve something. They wanted to renovate the apartment.

questions.prompt: We ____ in London and drove around for hours in the fog.
questions.explanation: “Got lost” means became unsure of the way. They could not find their destination.

questions.prompt: He was surprised when his boss told him, “I think it’s ____ you got a raise.”
questions.explanation: “High time” means an action is overdue. The boss thinks the employee should already have received a raise.

story.title: Idioms in context
paragraphs: Everybody knows that men hate to stop and ask for directions. My husband is no different. Every time we get lost, we drive around for hours before he finally pulls over and asks for help.

One Saturday we saw an ad in the newspaper for a country dance and picnic at a farm outside of town. We fixed up our old cowboy hats, cut out the map from the newspaper and started driving. After a few hours, I brought up the fact that we were lost. Of course my husband lost his temper when I suggested we ask someone for directions. “I can find it!” he yelled. I didn’t see any point in fighting about it, so I just told him, “By all means, carry on.”

After another hour of driving, I decided it was high time to ask for help. By chance we passed a little gas station with an old man sitting out by the pumps. My husband agreed to stop because we needed gas, but he drew the line at asking for directions. I got out of the car and walked over to the old man. Before I asked him anything he smiled and said, “The map is wrong. It’s Highway 23, not 32.” “How did you know?” I asked in surprise. “You’re the fifth woman whose husband has gotten lost in the last hour!”
